subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: After live current-main Copilot cron proof, should aborted/no-output Copilot runs enter model fallback, or should OpenClaw rely on the 60-second idle-timeout path plus cron error status?
rationale: Retrying an aborted isolated cron turn can recover message delivery, but it may also repeat work if tools or outbound side effects already happened, so the fallback boundary needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Prove first, keep fallback narrow
options.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof, then allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

options.title: Fallback on aborted no-output results
options.body: Classify aborted/no-output Copilot embedded results as fallback-worthy even when the stream ended without a terminal response.

options.title: Do not expand fallback
options.body: Keep current cron error surfacing and idle-timeout handling without adding a new aborted-result retry path.

recommendation.title: Prove first, keep fallback narrow
recommendation.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof, then allow fallback only for idle-timeout failures before tool or outbound side effects are observed.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history on the Copilot provider and stream seams where the remaining policy would likely land.
